_: Verdicts settled AFTER the research file and the batch plans. audit:multi-approach reads this last, so an entry here overrides them.

wa_mount_adams_wilson_glacier_headwall.why: East side from Cold Springs to camp in Avalanche Valley; no ascent from the north side is recorded. Row made consistent in leftovers 4 and 7.

wa_storm_king_north_face.why: The 1978 first ascent came up Park Creek to the Goode-Storm King saddle and rappelled onto the north-side glacier; nothing describes another way. Approach written in leftovers 7.

wa_mount_si_trail.why: Flagged FINISH only because the Haystack scramble sits on top of it; the trail is itself the one way in.

wa_mount_si_haystack_scramble.why: A finish on top of the Mount Si trail, and that trail is its only way in, so there is nothing to switch between.

wa_golden_horn_southwest_route.why: Flagged FINISH because the North Face row DESCENDS it back to Snowy Lakes; both start at Rainy Pass on the PCT, and nothing describes another way in.

wa_mount_rainier_mowich_face.why: Settled on the evidence, not left open: no page shows a party reaching the North Mowich from anywhere but Mowich Lake. The row already says the road there has been cut since the April 2025 Fairfax Bridge closure. Revisit only if an ascent account describes another start.

wa_mount_crowder_southwest_route.why: Every way to Crowder is a multi-day Pickets traverse (Goodell Creek, Big Beaver/Access Creek, or the Bacon Creek enchainment), all meeting at Wild Pass. A card per traverse start would describe traverses, not ways to this route, and the row's text already names both of its corridors. Its Goodell/Access Creek text is unverified (not in Beckey vols 1-2) and needs the owner's vol 3.

wa_mount_persis_the_hexorcist.why: Nothing online describes how anyone reaches the north face, only the name and the first ascensionist. The row's approach already says the base is reached cross-country, from the West Ridge path or the Anderson Creek side, and that the approach is not documented. With no documented way in, there is nothing to switch between.
